newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila business says peso depreciation not timely.
newsitem.headline: Manila business says peso depreciation not timely.

text.p: Any talk on devaluing the Philippine peso should be stopped to spare the local currency from further speculative attack, Federation of Philippine Industries (FPI) president Raul Concepcion said on Wednesday.
FPI was one of the business groups which had called for a weaker peso to help exporters regain their competitiveness in the international market.
The proposal which was raised in a meeting earlier this month with President Fidel Ramos and trade officials triggered fierce debate regarding the Central Bank's foreign exchange policy.

"At this point in time, all sectors -- exporters, businessmen -- should have a moratorium on talks on devaluation of the peso ... Any talk at this point in time will be counter-productive," Concepcion told Reuters Financial Television.
The FPI wanted "the exchange rate to undergo a gradual adjustment in a well-calibrated manner based on market forces with minimal effects on inflation," Concepcion said.
He added that the timing of any adjustment should be "appropriate", without elaborating.
The peso fell prey to fresh attacks after a Singapore newspaper reported that the Philippine Central Bank's Monetary Board would take up the issue of devaluation at today's meeting.
Both Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson and Trade Secretary Cesar Bautista, the sources quoted by the report, denied any such plans.
Concepcion said the Central Bank's decision to defend the peso by raising overnight rates sharply would not affect businesses in the short-term.
"We can continue to have the high interest rates," he said.
Concepcion added that the present situation would also help the system flush out short-term foreign investments which made local financial markets volatile.
